transcript.text: Gas oven took ages to light tonight then went WHOOMPH and now the kitchen smells really strongly of gas even though I've turned it off. Is it safe to try again?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

ok I'm really panicking, the smell is still strong. The meter box is outside by the front door, should I turn it off there? It's rented and I can't get hold of the landlord tonight, and I don't have a CO alarm either.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
1. In the meter box, find the lever on the pipe going into the meter. This is the emergency control valve.
2. When the handle is in line with the pipe, the gas is on. Turn it a quarter turn so it sits across the pipe. That's off.
3. If it's stiff, don't force it, and don't stay at it if you feel unwell. Just leave it for the emergency engineer. Then ring 0800 111 999 now, from outside or from your mobile away from the kitchen. They'll come out, make it safe and usually cap off the oven. Tell your landlord in the morning. By law they have to get a Gas Safe engineer to repair it and check it before it's used again. - Keep the doors and windows open.
• Don't touch any light switches, plugs or the doorbell.
• No flames or cigarettes.
• Wait outside if the smell is strong. You don't have a CO alarm, so watch for headache, dizziness, nausea or unusual tiredness in anyone in the house. If anyone has those, get them into fresh air and call 111, or 999 if they're severe. As for the oven, please don't try to light it again. Slow lighting followed by a whoomph means gas built up before it caught. That usually points to an ignition or flame-safety fault, or a valve that's letting gas through, and a smell that lingers after it's off makes a leak more likely. None of that is safe to check yourself, and it's a Gas Safe engineer job. You're doing the right things. Get that call made and you'll have help on the way.

reading.symptom: delayed ignition with loud whoomph, strong gas smell

claimsRejected.claim: Customer is in a rented home
The call and the emergency visit are free.

candidates: Gas escaping from the oven burner or supply after a delayed ignition (ignition or flame-safety fault, or a leaking valve (high)
plan: They asked: "Should I turn the gas off at the meter box outside by the front door?" - answer that first.

Safety: they reported a gas smell earlier and were given the emergency advice. Do not repeat it. Do not suggest any check or use of the appliance; answer what they ask now, and make sure they know to keep following that advice until a Gas Safe engineer has made it safe.
The fault they reported is: "delayed ignition with loud whoomph, strong gas smell". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
